notes: Exploratory algae branch. Rechecked on 2026-07-03. The PubMed abstract explicitly states that Asteromonas gracilis grows from 0.5 M NaCl to saturation and that the specific growth rate is maximal between 0.5 and 2.5 M NaCl, so this row is accepted as a quantitatively supported species-level halophilic alga. NCBI Taxonomy recognizes taxid 3156. Although no NCBI Assembly hit was found, organism-level BioSample/SRA transcriptome records exist in the OneKP data stream, including SAMEA104171077 linked to ERS1830095 and source material identifier CCAC 0049 (M1491), so sequence-side presence is real even if a genome assembly is not yet available.

Exploratory algae branch. Added on 2026-07-04 during the broad cross-label pass. The primary physiology paper reports an optimum growth temperature of 45 C, an upper temperature limit of 55-56 C, and an optimum pH between 2 and 3, so this row is accepted as a thermophilic thermoacidophilic alga. NCBI Taxonomy recognizes taxid 2771, and NCBI Assembly provides downloadable genome/protein routes including GCA_026184775.1. Because the phenotype evidence is species-level rather than exact-strain matched to the current assembly strain DBV 063 E5, any retrieval should remain explicit as a species-level downloadable fallback.

Exploratory algae branch. Added on 2026-07-04 during the broad cross-label pass by recovering and revalidating an archived heat-side candidate. The cited context and temperature-acclimation papers support C. merolae 10D as a thermoacidophilic red alga from low-pH high-temperature environments, with optimal cultivation reported around pH 1.5-2.5 and temperature 42-45 C. NCBI Taxonomy recognizes taxid 45157, and NCBI Assembly provides a downloadable genome/protein route at GCA_011170005.1 for strain 10D-T. Because the phenotype-side strain is written as 10D while the current assembly strain is 10D-T, this should be treated as a strain-adjacent downloadable case with the alias caveat kept explicit.

Exploratory algae branch. Rechecked on 2026-07-03. The article abstract directly states that D. parva growth was examined across 0.5, 1, 2, 2.5, and 3.5 M NaCl and that 2.5 M NaCl was the optimal salinity condition, so this row is accepted as a halophilic alga. NCBI Taxonomy recognizes taxid 3048. Although no NCBI Assembly hit was found, organism-level BioSample SAMN46785405 links D. parva to strain FACHB-815, isolate Wri1_3, and SRA record SRS24057511, which gives a concrete sequence-side foothold for later retrieval work.

Exploratory algae branch. Rechecked on 2026-07-03. The PubMed abstract for D. salina SA 134 reports a tested salinity range of 0.5-2.5 M NaCl and maximum growth at 1.5-2.0 M NaCl, so this row is accepted as a strain-backed halophilic alga. NCBI Taxonomy recognizes taxid 3046, and NCBI Assembly provides reference-genome accession GCA_002284615.2 for D. salina strain CCAP 19/18; because this is not the same strain as SA 134, any sequence retrieval is treated as a species-level fallback rather than an exact-strain match.

Exploratory algae branch. Rechecked on 2026-07-03. The PubMed abstract explicitly states that growth rates were reduced at 0.05 and 3.0 mol/L NaCl and that optimum salinities were 0.2-0.5 mol/L NaCl, so this row is accepted as a species-level saline-adapted alga. NCBI Taxonomy recognizes taxid 3047, and NCBI Assembly provides sequence-linked identities including CCAP 19/42 and UTEX 999 for later retrieval decisions.

Exploratory algae branch. Added on 2026-07-04 during the broad cross-label pass and promoted on 2026-07-04 during the second broad pass. The PubMed abstract explicitly reports optimal conditions of 40 C and pH 3 for strain Galdieri Merola 002, so this row is accepted as a high-temperature thermoacidophilic alga under the separate exploratory algae criteria. NCBI Taxonomy recognizes taxid 130081. Although the newest ACUF 002 assembly route GCA_057165425.1 did not provide a verified protein FASTA, NCBI also provides older annotated species-level assemblies including GCF_000341285.1 strain 074W and GCA_024341865.1 strain NIES-3638(074W), both with expected protein FASTA paths returning HTTP 200 on 2026-07-04. Retrieval should therefore proceed as an explicit species-level downloadable fallback rather than an exact-strain match.

Exploratory algae branch. Added on 2026-07-03 during the post-cleanup saline-adapted pass. The primary paper reports that the best performance was achieved when 18 g/L sea salt was added into crude soda solution, corresponding to salinity 25 per mille; this was stored as a seawater-equivalent NaCl proxy of about 0.43 M for the exploratory branch. NCBI Taxonomy recognizes taxid 145522, and NCBI Assembly provides multiple downloadable genome/protein routes, including GCA_037830525.2 for strain CCAP849/10. Because the phenotype-side evidence is species-level rather than exact-strain matched to the selected assembly, any sequence retrieval should remain explicit as a species-level downloadable fallback.

Exploratory algae branch. Rechecked on 2026-07-03. The Nature paper provides explicit saline-growth evidence, with no statistical difference in growth rate at 35 versus 50 PPT marine salts and robust growth up to 100 PPT; 35 PPT was stored as a seawater-equivalent NaCl proxy. NCBI Taxonomy recognizes taxid 2695429 as Picochlorum sp. 'celeri', and NCBI Assembly provides accession GCA_010909725.1 linked to BioSample SAMN13721886. Because no strain or isolate is collected in the BioSample metadata, this row is accepted as a species-level sequence fallback rather than an exact-strain match.

Exploratory algae branch. Promoted on 2026-07-03 as a saline-adapted named-study-strain alga. The primary strain paper supports broad salinity tolerance and thermotolerance, and the exploratory branch continues the prior project practice of accepting defensible strain-adjacent sequence links when the sequence-side record is close but not perfectly label-matched. NCBI Taxonomy uses Picochlorum renovo (nom. nud.) taxid 2601844 and NCBI Assembly links GCA_009650465.1 to BioSample SAMN12509183, where the strain is recorded as NREL1; this alias gap relative to phenotype-side NREL 39-A8 must remain explicit in downstream notes.

Exploratory algae branch. Added on 2026-07-05 during the branch-expansion step as a psychrophilic alga with an explicit low-temperature optimum near 4 C. The earlier saline-adapted interpretation was removed because it depended on habitat inference rather than an explicit measured salinity optimum, which conflicts with the branch rule against habitat-only salinity labeling. NCBI Assembly provides downloadable accession GCA_001750085.1 for strain CCMP1102.

Exploratory algae branch. Added on 2026-07-05 during the branch-expansion step as a psychrophilic green alga with an explicit low-temperature optimum near 5 C. The row is carried as a named-strain downloadable case linked to RefSeq assembly GCF_000258705.1.

include_in_core: Exploratory algae branch. Added on 2026-07-05 during the branch-expansion step as a non-thermophilic acidophilic green alga with an explicit pH optimum near 1.0. The supporting source is the Chlamydomonas eustigma genome paper in PNAS, and the row is linked to downloadable NCBI assembly GCA_002335675.1.
